title: Bengal health department show-causes Calcutta Medical College interns over stampede remarks
dek: The interns told reporters after the Chorbagan crowd crush that patients were being sent to private hospitals and that life-saving medicines were short. The department denies the shortage; doctors' leaders call the notices political revenge.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
West Bengal's health department has issued show-cause notices to eight interns at Calcutta Medical College and Hospital over remarks they made to reporters after the Chorbagan Durga Puja stampede, in which they questioned the hospital's facilities and alleged that patients were being referred to private hospitals, according to reports. The interns have three days to explain themselves.

Health Minister Sharadwat Mukherjee confirmed the notices, and Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said it should be examined whether the interns were on duty when they spoke, since doing so would breach service rules, according to reports. Two of the best-known faces of the 2024 junior doctors' movement in Kolkata called the action "political revenge".

## What the notices say

The notices accuse the interns of speaking to the media instead of attending to their duties while on duty, according to reports. After the crowd crush at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin pandal in north Kolkata in October, which killed 19 people and injured at least 25, the interns told reporters that senior government officials had instructed hospitals to refer patients to private facilities and that the hospital lacked essential life-saving medicines.

The health department has rejected the claim of a medicine shortage, and the state government has defended moving injured stampede victims to private hospitals, saying it was done to give them better treatment and prevent more deaths, according to reports. One report put the number of interns at eight in one place and nine in another; the hospital principal is reported to have written to the guardians of the interns concerned.

## What each side says

One of the interns said he had not been on duty when he spoke to reporters. "We have been served a show-cause notice and asked to submit an explanation. However, I was not on duty that day," he said, according to reports. Responding to the department's denial of a shortage, he said, "All doctors here know the actual situation."

Mr Mukherjee said the authorities had issued the notices because they felt rules may have been broken, and that the interns would reply, according to reports. He separately warned junior doctors at Barasat Medical College that action would follow allegations that they had pressured patients' families to buy medicines from particular shops.

Debasish Halder and Aniket Mahato, two doctors who led the 2024 protests by junior doctors over the rape and murder of a trainee doctor at RG Kar Medical College and Hospital, called the notices "political revenge", according to reports.

## Background

The 2024 RG Kar case set off weeks of protests and a work stoppage by junior doctors in government hospitals across West Bengal, who demanded safer workplaces and complained of intimidation in medical colleges. Their complaints about how government hospitals are run, from staffing to supplies, have remained a sensitive political issue.

The Chorbagan stampede has become the first major test of the BJP government that took office in May. The state has since issued safety rules for Kali Puja, Jagaddhatri Puja and Chhath, including better lighting at pandals and controlled entry for visitors. A special investigation team has been asked to report on the stampede within three months, according to reports.

## What happens next

The interns' replies are due within three days. The department has not said what action it could take if it finds their explanations unsatisfactory.
